sections.title: Current conclusion
sections.markdown:
**Original-register review, 31 October 2026:** James’s parent cell is blank in the original 1860 death return. It confirms the existing 28 September date, age, cooper trade and Susan as wife/informant. The row does not expressly repeat a birthplace; that remains an index/transcription attribution. His father remains **Unknown**, without a percentage.

**31 October 2026:** The original 1819 Hendrick–Eudaly bond and bride’s declaration have now been read. William Glasgo is the surety and a declaration witness; no parent or kinship is stated. James’s father remains **Unknown**, without a percentage. The 1815/1819 Elizabeth identity and William’s later identity remain open, as assessed below.

Reviewed30October2026: The original depositions taken at the Exchange Hotel in Danville on 1 October 1851 name James Glasgow and William Glasgow. James says he was a neighbour of Leonard Fitzgerald in 1821 and recalls renting part of the Little Fall Creek property around 1826 through an agent. William separately says he was Fitzgerald’s neighbour in 1821 and thinks Fitzgerald remained there in 1827, while expressly not being positive. Both signatures appear. The testimony gives neither Glasgow man’s age, occupation, spouse or parents and does not call the two men relatives. James Glasgow-62, the Pittsylvania cooper, is the leading existing compatible candidate for the James deponent, not a proved identification. Same county, sustained local knowledge and the existing1840deponent comparison support investigation; no family identifier links them. William’s identity and any kinship with James, the1815declarant Robert or Elizabeth remain unresolved. No duplicate person, father candidate, parent attachment, vital change or confidence gain is created. The original1850Danville census separately confirms the already indexed cooper household. See the dated source review below.

Reviewed 30 October 2026: **James’s father remains unknown.** The inspected 1860 death transcription records a cooper aged 71 years 10 months 12 days, “killed,” with wife Susan as informant; it names no parent. The contributed Robert Glasgow/Sarah Cooper pedigree remains unproved.

Original checked 31 October 2026: the parent field is blank; the full source review below supersedes the earlier uninspected status. A 16 November 1788 birthday calculated from the transcribed age and the separately indexed 28 September 1860 date is not independent birth evidence. All parent and structured vital fields are preserved. The 1815 Eudaley/Glasgow papers remain a local-family test. Corrected30October: Robert Glasgow signed an age declaration; Herod Worsham, not Robert, was the bond surety. No relationship to James is established.

Reviewed 27 October 2026: an original Danville deposition names James Glasgow on 8 April 1840. This is a compatible candidate for the Pittsylvania cooper, but the testimony gives no age, occupation or family identifier. It does not identify his parents or change the parentage assessment.

sections.title: Danville deposition — 27 October 2026
sections.markdown:
The [original deposition](https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box041/143_1841_001_0021.pdf), with its [attestation](https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box041/143_1841_001_0022.pdf), records James Glasgow and Roderick R. Hudnall at the National Hotel in Danville on **8 April 1840**. It belongs to Pittsylvania chancery case **1841-001**, James M. Sutherlin and wife against Armistead G. Weir, written “Wier” in the deposition caption. The case’s closing year is not the deposition date.

James says that in 1836 he heard Weir say he had bought fodder from Sutherlin; he thought the quantity was two stacks. He also gives an opinion of a stack’s value. The page bears a signature reading **James Glasgow**. This is witness testimony about another man’s purchase, not evidence that James bought or sold the fodder. Hudnall’s separate answer follows; it must not be attributed to James.

The name and court locality fit this James, whose held profile cites an 1840 Pittsylvania census, but the manuscript supplies **no age, occupation, residence, spouse or parent** to establish the match. Retain Glasgow-62 as a compatible candidate. The separate Virginia-born [James M. Glasgow-193](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-193) and [James William Glasgow-2925](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2925) have held Ohio and Tennessee household accounts; those locations alone do not exclude a temporary Danville appearance. No duplicate person or new family connection is proposed.

A [notice dated 6 April 1840](https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box041/143_1841_001_0034.pdf) names James Glasgow and Roderick R. Hudnall and schedules their depositions for Wednesday the 8th at the National Hotel in Danville. It corroborates the date and venue of the already inspected testimony; it is not a second May appearance and adds no family identifier.

Across the initial and follow-up batches, **84 of the case’s 89 scans were visually reviewed**. Images **46, 47, 57, 58 and 61 remain unread** after rendering failures; faint or damaged writing elsewhere further limits negative conclusions. A background-only extraction from image 46 was not counted as a reading. Suspected Glasgow readings on images 78–80 were checked against the images and rejected as Haynes or Sutherlin. No complete-case absence claim is made. The 1818 original bond has since been inspected (30 October review below). Signature comparison and the separate 1815 family-identification test remain open.

sections.title: Pittsylvania death and parent-claim review — 23 October 2026
sections.markdown:
The inspected [USGenWeb 1860 Pittsylvania death transcription](https://www.usgenwebsites.org/vagenweb/pittsylvania/deaths/1860Deaths.htm) records James Glasgow, cooper, age 71 years 10 months 12 days, Pittsylvania birthplace, cause **“killed,”** and Susan Glasgow as informant and wife. Its parent column and exact death-date cell are blank. This is a modern transcription of county returns; the original register was not inspected. The existing 28 September 1860 date comes from the previously cited death index, FHL 2048580. potential_parentage.method: Automated leads use birth surnames—not married surnames—as parental eligibility, role-specific biological age limits, bounded and approximate-date uncertainty, household chronology, specific time-aware localities, mapped distance, tenancy succession, migration destinations and sex-aware Scottish naming positions across generations. People already attached as the subject's parents stay in the identity summary and are excluded from this alternative-candidate list, regardless of relationship confidence. The main calibration uses clues available on disconnected profiles; existing parent and sibling links are retained as comparison context rather than treated as transferable evidence. Common ordered names and grandparent-to-child echoes receive a small non-zero weight, so a John or James match can support several independent criteria without producing a lead alone. Rare names, repeated bearers and bundles across otherwise distinct branches receive substantially more weight according to catalogue frequency. An exact migration place is weighted by its rarity and repetition across both branches; a shared destination country is worth only one point. Extra weight is added only when at least three independent clue types converge: naming, locality, specific migration, household chronology or collateral networks. Sparse profiles retain a clearly labelled chronology-only fallback instead of disappearing. Countries, states, counties and research clusters do not count as a shared locality, and fallback, broad representative or kin-inferred coordinates are excluded from distance scoring. Shared descendant profiles are removed before branch-name comparison. A candidate already recorded as a parent-in-law is excluded. A confident or independently supported parent is treated as settled; uncertain and unassessed attachments remain open to alternative comparison. A different linked parent, an uncle/aunt or grandparent path, and a matching existing child profile prevent an alternative from being classified as a strong direct-parent lead until the underlying tree conflict or duplicate is resolved. Familiar forms such as Bessie are normalised. Surname remains an eligibility filter worth zero points.
potential_parentage.warning: Naming customs, shared farms and occupations are circumstantial. Children, spouses and collateral relatives may be missing, and tree-derived family networks are not independent evidence. Scores rank research leads; they do not prove parentage.

Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-2925|James William Glasgow]] have Ohio and Tennessee household accounts; geography alone does not exclude travel to Danville. This source establishes no new parent or exact vital date for the profile.

=== Original marriage bond checked — 30 October 2026 ===

The original bond confirms that James Glasgow obtained a licence to marry Susanah High on 21 October 1818. James Glasgow and Freeman High are the obligors; James signs his name and Freeman’s entry bears his mark. R. Hopkins is the witness. No parent, age or occupation of James is stated.<ref>Pittsylvania County, Virginia, original marriage bonds, 1816–1820, FamilySearch DGS 007741064, item 3 (1818), [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-YQ6X-J image 270 of 281, James Glasgow/Susanah High bond], 21 October 1818; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-YQCW-C preceding endorsement, image 269]. Original images visually inspected 30 October 2026; bond image downloaded.</ref> This confirms the earlier compilation, without establishing James’s father, Freeman’s kinship to the bride, or the identity of the 1840 deponent.

=== Original 1815 roles and signature comparison — 30 October 2026 ===

The original 22 December 1815 bond names Robert Eudaley and Herod Worsham as obligors; both signature entries bear marks. Robert Glasgow instead signed the separate declaration that Elizabeth was of age and willing to marry. The typed compilation’s Robert Glasgow bondsman entry is contradicted by the original bond. Neither original states that Robert was Elizabeth’s father or that Elizabeth was James’s sister.<ref>Pittsylvania County, Virginia, original marriage bonds, FamilySearch DGS007741063, item2: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-R33H-Y bond front, full-film image311/item image175]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-R33H-2 endorsement, image310]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-R334-N Robert Glasgow declaration, image309/item image173]. === Little Fall Creek witness network — 30 October 2026 ===

The original depositions taken at the Exchange Hotel in Danville on 1 October 1851 name James Glasgow and William Glasgow. James says he was a neighbour of Leonard Fitzgerald in 1821 and recalls renting part of the Little Fall Creek property around 1826 through an agent. William separately says he was Fitzgerald’s neighbour in 1821 and thinks Fitzgerald remained there in 1827, while expressly not being positive. Both signatures appear. The testimony gives neither Glasgow man’s age, occupation, spouse or parents and does not call the two men relatives.<ref>Library of Virginia, Pittsylvania chancery1854-055, James Lanier v. Anderson Kirby etc., depositions taken1October1851: [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0023.pdf scan23, opening/date], [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0024.pdf scan24] and [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0025.pdf scan25, James’s testimony], [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0026.pdf scan26, James’s signature and William’s testimony/signature]. === Original Hendrick–Eudaly packet — 31 October 2026 ===

The original Pittsylvania bond of 1 February 1819 names Nathaniel Hendrick and William Glasgo as obligors for Nathaniel’s licence to marry Elizabeth Eudaly. Both names appear in the signature entries; William’s surname there is written Glasgow. The associated declaration, dated 30 January 1819 in Elizabeth Eudaly’s name, states that she has no objection to Nathaniel obtaining a marriage licence to marry her. William Glasgo is named under the witness heading. The matching endorsement reads Hendrick, marriage bond, to the Governor.

These originals confirm the previously indexed William association and add the bride’s dated declaration. They name no parent or relationship between William, Elizabeth and James Glasgow-62. The 1819 bride is a specific possible continuation of the Elizabeth Glasgow who obtained a licence with Robert Eudaley in this county in December 1815: the given name, unusual married surname and continuing Glasgow associates fit. Neither packet calls her a widow or recites the earlier marriage, so that identity remains a candidate, not a proved remarriage or evidence of Robert’s death. A non-expert visual comparison of the 1819 and 1851 William signatures is compatible in broad cursive forms, but not diagnostic; the surety is not identified as the Little Fall Creek deponent or with any particular existing William profile. Existing William-3678 and William-563 remain weak unselected comparisons; their separate Wythe and Ohio accounts supply no specific Pittsylvania bridge. James’s father remains Unknown and unrated. No family attachment, vital field or confidence rating changes.<ref>Pittsylvania County, Virginia, original marriage bonds, FamilySearch DGS 007741064: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-YQH5-B full-film image 837, Elizabeth Eudaly declaration, 30 January 1819]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-YQ69-6 image 838, Hendrick endorsement]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-YQDP-1 image 839, Nathaniel Hendrick / Elizabeth Eudaly bond, 1 February 1819]. The original Pittsylvania death register for 1860 has now been inspected at FamilySearch DGS 004225404, full-film image 316, entry indexed as the 37th. James Glasgow’s row records 28 September, cause “Killed,” age 71 years 10 months 12 days, and occupation cooper. Susan Glasgow is the named informant, explicitly described as his wife. The Names of Parents cell on James’s row is blank. The parent names on the immediately preceding John Gammon row do not belong to James.

No birthplace wording or ditto mark is visible in James’s own Where Born cell in the inspected row; the held Pittsylvania birthplace remains an index/transcription attribution, not a newly confirmed literal entry on this image. The county appears in the register heading. The consort column likewise does not supply a named spouse; Susan is identified through the informant columns. The full age is reported information, not a birth-register entry: calculating a birthday from it does not create independent birth evidence.
